fields.Name: informz
fields.Description: Higher Logic Thrive Marketing Professional (formerly Informz) — email-marketing/AMS platform. Single-operation SOAP AAPI (PostInformzMessage): GridRequest (read) and ActionRequest (write) XML documents for subscriber, mailing, and campaign data.

universalPK.note: No vendor-wide 'id' convention exists — this is NOT a REST/JSON API with a uniform PK field name. 68/70 documented grids have an *_id field candidate (per SOURCE_STUDY.md Step 2b, script sources/scripts/classify-grids.mjs) whose description explicitly says 'ID in Informz' / the vendor-internal identifier (preferred over any 'Unique remote ID' field, which is the TENANT'S OWN correlation key back to their source AMS — a natural FK/business-key, not Informz's PK). The 2 grids without an *_id PK candidate: accounting_code (natural key 'code', a String) and email_block_status (a brand-scoped singleton status record with no row identity — 3 fields only). This is a per-IO PK census summary for runtime SoftPKClassifier reference; each IO's own IsPrimaryKey selection is ioiof-extractor's job with its own evidence.
universalPK.fieldNameConvention: <object_singular>_id (e.g. subscriber_id, mailing_id, interest_id) — NOT a bare 'id'

Transport.note: Confirmed live: the WSDL (https://partner.informz.net/aapi/InformzService.svc?wsdl) declares exactly ONE operation, PostInformzMessage(string) — a single opaque XML-in-a-string SOAP envelope, not a resource-per-endpoint REST shape. The base URL is REGION-selected from this fixed 3-entry vendor table, NEVER per-tenant — the tenant is identified purely by the <Brand id> + <User>/<Password> credential embedded IN the posted document body, never by the host. No tenant value is baked here. Source: API General Information article (360033049191, 'API endpoints' section) — endpoints verbatim; corroborated live by SourceAuditor's WSDL fetch (SOURCES.json entry, AccessStatus: Reachable).

DocumentShapes.note: Two XML document types, both POSTed as the single string argument to PostInformzMessage. Skeletons below are reproduced verbatim from the vendor's own published Request/Response samples (API General Information article 360033049191 for the top-level ActionRequest/GridRequest wrapper; Grid Requests Overview 360033049251, Grid Requests Conditions Block 360032692452, and Grid Requests Usage Pattern 360032692472 for the Grids/Conditions/ReturnFields inner shape and the GridResponse read shape).

GridRequest.multiGrid: A single GridRequest document MAY contain multiple <Grid type="..."> blocks under one <Grids> parent — each is an independent request/response pair evaluated in the same round-trip (documented + sample-evidenced in Grid Requests Conditions Block, 'Grid Requests with multiple grids').

GridResponse.emptyResultShape: <Grid type="<grid_token>" /> (self-closing, zero <Record> children) when no rows match — confirmed sample in Grid Requests Usage Pattern ('Response 2: When No Rows are Returned').
GridResponse.recordRowNumbering: Record row numbering is 1-based in most samples but one authoritative sample (Grid Requests Conditions Block, Count example) shows row="0" for a single-row Count response — row numbering is not a reliable ordinal contract across all grids; do not assume 0- or 1-based universally.

ActionRequest.note: Per-action element shape (e.g. <CreateMailing>, <BulkUpload>, <Subscribe>) is documented individually per ActionRequest article and NOT re-derived here — see ActionCatalog / the 9 ActionRequests articles cited in SOURCE_STUDY.md Step 7. Node order within an action element is XSD-driven and UNDISCOVERABLE (no downloadable XSD found anywhere in the 212-article corpus) — the connector MUST preserve the exact element order shown in each action's own published Request sample, not invent an order.

userVsUsernameDiscrepancy.verdict: USE <User>, NOT <Username>, in both GridRequest and ActionRequest bodies. This is the form every dedicated, per-endpoint documented Request/Response sample in the corpus uses.
userVsUsernameDiscrepancy.evidence: The ONLY place <Username> appears anywhere in the 212-article corpus is the two illustrative top-level skeleton snippets in the single general-overview article 'API General Information' (360033049191) — one ActionRequest skeleton and one GridRequest skeleton, both using <Username>testuser</Username>. Every other sample in the corpus — ALL grid articles read (Grid Requests Conditions Block 360032692452, Grid Requests Usage Pattern 360032692472, Sample Message Encryption/Compression 360044600992, GridRequests - Subscriber Interests Changes and Deletions 360032692232) AND all 3 ActionRequest articles independently grepped for the tag (Create Mailing MD1 360032692272, BulkUpload 360032692112, Subscribe/Unsubscribe/Optout 360032692392) — use <User>...</User> exclusively, in both Request and Response samples. 20+ independent <User> occurrences vs 2 <Username> occurrences (both in the same single overview article). The credential-type schema (metadata/credential-types/schemas/informz-api.schema.json) already hedges 'embedded ... as <User> or <Username>' — this resolves the hedge: emit <User>.
userVsUsernameDiscrepancy.residualDoubt: No downloadable XSD confirms server-side tolerance for <Username> as an alias; if a live credentialed probe ever proves the server also accepts <Username>, that would just make <User> a documented-preferred synonym, not wrong. Absent that probe, <User> is the evidence-backed choice.

Pagination.note: Universal, vendor-wide mechanism — confirmed in Grid Requests Overview (360033049251: 'Each request can return a maximum of 1,000 rows' + the SortField/StartRow/NumberOfRows paging section) and reproduced identically in Grid Requests Conditions Block (360032692452) and Grid Requests Usage Pattern (360032692472, 5 worked request/response pairs demonstrating StartRow=0/51 with NumberOfRows=50). SOURCE_STUDY.md Step 2b confirms this is per-vendor, not per-grid: 'Paging is universal, not per-grid ... every grid in the catalog is subject to the SAME generic SortField/StartRow/NumberOfRows mechanism ... no grid article documents an exception.' `Count` is requested as the sole <DataElement> in ReturnFields (with a <Count /> self-closing tag noted in Grid Requests Conditions Block) to get a total-row count for planning pagination BEFORE paging through data — not returned automatically alongside a normal row page. OBLIGATION: offset paging over a live, continuously-mutating table drifts (rows inserted/deleted between page N and N+1 shift the StartRow window) unless the request pins a stable SortField on a monotonic/unique key — the connector must ALWAYS send an explicit SortField, never rely on server-default ordering, and should prefer a field that is effectively append-only/immutable per row (e.g. the grid's own *_id or a creation timestamp) over a mutable field.

Conditions.collectionOperatorWireNote: Prose describes the 4th operator as 'Not In' / 'NOT IN' but the actual wire token in every XML sample is the single word NOTIN (no space) — e.g. Grid Requests Conditions Block Example 2: <SetOperator>NOTIN</SetOperator>. Emit NOTIN literally, not 'NOT IN'.
Conditions.between: <Condition><Between><DataElement>field</DataElement><DataValue>from</DataValue><DataValue>to</DataValue></Between></Condition> — the earlier (from) DataValue MUST be listed before the later (to) DataValue (explicit vendor TIP in both Grid Requests Overview and Grid Requests Conditions Block).
Conditions.timeRequirement: When using EQ or IN with a DateTime DataElement, a time-of-day component is REQUIRED in the DataValue; it is optional for all other comparators/operators. If time is omitted, it defaults to 00:00:00 UTC. (Grid Requests Overview 360033049251, Grid Requests Conditions Block 360032692452 — both state this identically.)
multiConditionRules: Each condition's <DataElement> can appear only ONCE in a request — a repeated DataElement across two <Condition> blocks conflicts and returns zero fields (explicit vendor warning, Grid Requests Conditions Block 'Grid Requests with multiple conditions').
Each condition needs its own <Condition> parent tag.
Work large-to-small: expect fewer records as more conditions are added.
Conditions.role: This IS the incremental-sync mechanism — see Incremental below. Evidence: Grid Requests Overview (360033049251), Grid Requests Conditions Block (360032692452, full Comparators/Operators/Between tables + 3 worked multi-condition examples), Grid Requests Usage Pattern (360032692472, 5 worked request/response pairs).

Incremental.mechanism: A GTE (or Between, for a bounded window) Condition on a grid's own DateTime-typed DataElement, re-sent on each sync with an advancing watermark value, IS the incremental-sync mechanism for this vendor — there is no separate cursor/delta-token/webhook primitive. Confirmed pattern from Grid Requests Usage Pattern's worked examples (GTE/LT bracketing on Mailing_Date) and Grid Requests Conditions Block Example 3 (Between on create_date).
Incremental.coverageGap: 35/70 documented grids have ZERO DateTime-typed fields at all (verified per-grid by classify-grids.mjs, e.g. subscriber_personal_information: 29 fields, all Int/String, no date field) — these 35 grids have NO vendor-native incremental watermark; a connector must fall back to full-refresh or content-hash idempotency for them. Of the 35 that DO have a candidate, confidence is tiered: HIGH (1 grid, `subscriber` — an explicit 'last modified'-shaped field), MEDIUM (a named event/creation/mailing timestamp, correct for append-only event-log-shaped grids like opens/clicks/bounces where a row is never mutated after the event), LOW (any other DateTime field, unclassified semantics — do not assume it is a modified-at watermark without per-grid confirmation).

timestampSemantics.storageTZ: Eastern Standard Time (EST) — all date/time information is stored in the Thrive Marketing Professional database in EST.
timestampSemantics.wireTZ: UTC — when pulled via the API, EST is CONVERTED to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) before being returned. Every returned timestamp carries a trailing 'Z' UTC indicator and is already fully converted; the connector must NOT apply any further timezone offset to a value read from a GridResponse.
timestampSemantics.dstWarning: UTC never adjusts for Daylight Saving Time, so the EST↔UTC offset used internally by the vendor VARIES across the year (4 hours in EDT months, 5 hours in EST months) — this is purely a vendor-internal storage detail; since the API always returns already-UTC-normalized 'Z' timestamps, a correctly-implemented connector treating every returned value as literal UTC is unaffected by the DST swing. The risk is only for a connector author who mistakenly re-applies an EST offset to an already-UTC value.

historyWindowSplit.pattern: Exactly ONE documented pair in the whole 70-grid catalog: subscriber_mailing_history (mailings/activity sent to a subscriber WITHIN THE PAST 100 DAYS) vs subscriber_mailing_history_all (mailings sent MORE THAN 100 days ago). These are NOT superset/subset — _all explicitly EXCLUDES the last 100 days, it is the complement, not a full-history union. A connector that wants complete history for this family MUST read BOTH grids and union the results; reading only one silently omits either the recent window or everything before it.
historyWindowSplit.citation: GridRequests - Subscriber Mailing and Summary Histories, article 360032692212 ('within the past 100 days' / 'more than 100 days ago', both stated verbatim in the article body).

transportLayer.shape: All application-level exceptions are returned as a SOAP Fault of type InformzAAPIFault, carrying a machine-readable camelCase `code` (a generic error-class string) and a human-readable `reason` string.
transportLayer.httpStatus: A SOAP Fault is delivered as HTTP 500 (standard SOAP-over-HTTP behavior) — the connector's ClassifyError must inspect the SOAP Fault body on a 500 response rather than treating every 500 as a transport failure.
transportLayer.codesNonExhaustiveWarning: The vendor's own article title for this table is 'The following table lists SOME possible SOAP fault codes' — explicitly non-exhaustive. ClassifyError must NOT assume this is the complete code space; unrecognized `code` values should fall through to a generic-fault handler, not be treated as a parse error.

inResponseErrorNodes.note: Searched all 212 pinned article bodies for an in-band error/fault node pattern inside a 200-status GridResponse/ActionResponse (e.g. an <Error>/<ErrorMessage>/<ErrorCode> element) — none found. The only error-carrying mechanism documented anywhere in the corpus is the SOAP Fault described above. A 200-status response with a self-closing empty <Grid type="..." /> is a legitimate ZERO-ROW result, not an error (see DocumentShapes.GridResponse.emptyResultShape).

AuthPreconditions.note: Higher Logic validates the Brand against a REGISTERED IP address; correct credentials from an unregistered egress IP fail. Provisioning requires a Higher Logic support case. Evidence for the requirement itself: API General Information (360033049191, 'Document notes' — 'Brand id: your unique account ID; when the document is received, this is validated against the IP address that is stored with your brand in order to ensure that it is a valid origin point.') and the SOAP Fault code NoAvailableIPAddressException (SOAP Fault Error Codes, 360044601092), which is consistent with an IP-gated brand model. The dedicated 'Required IP Addresses for Allowlisting' article (found at articleId 28371220360852 in the walked corpus) is itself a Zendesk-level DUPLICATE stub whose body reads 'This article is a duplicate. The original article is located at: https://support.higherlogic.com/hc/en-us/articles/28344411130388' — that redirect target (28344411130388) was NOT captured by the corpus snapshot (outside the 212-article walk), so the SPECIFIC IP range/allowlist procedure text is a genuine gap, not evidenced here; only the REQUIREMENT itself (Brand-to-IP validation) is evidenced.

CustomFieldModel.note: Subscriber DEMOGRAPHICS, EXTENDED DEMOGRAPHICS and INTERESTS are TENANT-DEFINED — each Informz/Thrive Marketing Professional Brand defines its own demographic-field and interest set in its own admin UI; the help-center corpus documents the GRID SHAPE (the wrapper: subscriber_id, personal_information_id/name/value, interest_id/name, etc.) but NEVER a fixed, vendor-wide enumeration of the demographic/interest NAMES themselves — those are per-brand data, not part of the API contract. They MUST be reached at runtime as per-connection Discovered/custom data via the framework's runtime discovery + custom-column capture path — NEVER baked as vendor-wide Declared columns from any one brand's observed set. Evidence: GridRequests - Subscriber Demographics and Extended Demographic (360032692132), GridRequests - Subscriber Personal Information and Persona (360032692352), GridRequests - Subscriber Interests, Changes, and Deletions (360032692232) — all document the wrapper shape (an ID/name/value triple pattern) with no fixed name enumeration.

Configuration.DiscoveryIsAuthoritativeNote: There is NO describe-all/introspection endpoint in this API (the single operation is PostInformzMessage(string); nothing enumerates the live set of Grid/Action types a credential can access). The 70-grid / 9-action catalog in this build is the vendor's PUBLISHED documentation set, not a live introspection result — a brand's actual permissioned surface could be a subset (feature-gated) or, in principle, carry Informz-side additions not yet documented publicly. Absence of a grid/action/field at runtime discovery therefore proves nothing about the vendor's true capability set — NOTHING may ever be deactivated purely on a discovery-time absence signal for this connector.

WriteCapability.note: NOT a read-only/pull-only vendor. 9 documented ActionRequest operations across 4 families, classified with evidence in SOURCE_STUDY.md Step 7 (packages/Integration/connectors-registry/informz/SOURCE_STUDY.md).
WriteCapability.bulkJobNote: BulkUpload is explicitly documented as ASYNCHRONOUS, for >1,000-row subscriber-list transfers, with 5 processing modes (AddOrUpdateSubscribers/ReplaceAllSubscribers/RemoveSubscribers/UnsubscribeSubscribers/ResubscribeSubscribers) and vendor text noting 'there is a delay of a few minutes between when the call is received and acknowledged' — not mappable to a synchronous per-operation CreateRecord/UpdateRecord; it needs a bulk-job code path, distinct from Subscribe's synchronous per-record path (vendor explicitly steers high-volume callers from Subscribe toward BulkUpload: 'If you expect to be regularly updating subscriber data, Informz recommends the BulkUpload method... processed synchronously' [sic, contrasting Subscribe's low-volume-only guidance]).
WriteCapability.citation: ActionRequests - Create Mailing (MD1) 360032692272; ActionRequests - Create Message (MD2) 360038003251; ActionRequests - BulkUpload 360032692112; ActionRequests - BulkUpload with Interests 360045044011; ActionRequests - Subscribe, Unsubscribe, and Opt Out 360032692392; ActionRequests - Update Contact Message Category Preference 52916120177044.

Configuration.ConcurrencyControlNote: No ETag/version/If-Match/If-Unmodified-Since mechanism, or any per-record version/revision field, is documented anywhere in the 212-article corpus for either GridResponse read rows or ActionRequest writes. Optimistic-concurrency conflict resolution is not available; any bidirectional conflict handling for this vendor is snapshot/3-way-diff only, never a real MostRecent-by-version comparison.

DeleteSemantics.note: No general 'deleted subscriber' feed exists anywhere in the documented catalog — deleting/purging a subscriber record itself has no corresponding grid. HOWEVER, two grids DO expose a deletion-shaped signal, scoped narrowly to Interest (topic/target-group) MEMBERSHIP, not the subscriber record itself: (1) get_subscriber_interest_changes — an Added/Removed event-log keyed by an `action` field (values 'Added'/'Removed') plus `action_date`, filterable by a required Start/End date window; (2) subscriber_interests_deleted — a point-in-time snapshot of subscribers currently removed-from-interest, carrying a deleted_from_interest_date field. Both are Interest-association tombstone/event signals, not a subscriber-record deletion feed. A sync that relies on either for 'has this subscriber been deleted' would be wrong; they only answer 'has this subscriber's Interest membership changed.'
DeleteSemantics.citation: GridRequests - Subscriber Interests, Changes, and Deletions, article 360032692232 (both grids' typed Data-Element tables + worked Request/Response samples read directly).

Configuration.DefaultSyncDirectionNote: Every new EntityMap for this connector should default to Pull (read-only), per project discipline — bidirectional write access is opt-in only, gated on a sandbox-validated `allowWrite`, never a build-time default, regardless of the documented WriteCapability above.
Configuration.DefaultConflictResolutionNote: IF bidirectional sync is later explicitly enabled for a given object (never by default — see DefaultSyncDirection), recommend SourceWins (Informz-side data wins over the destination) rather than MostRecent or DestWins: ConcurrencyControl is 'none' (no ETag/version), so there is no reliable per-record revision signal to arbitrate a true 'most recent' decision, and Manual resolution has no documented vendor-side moderation queue to route conflicts through for this API. SourceWins is the conservative default until a per-vendor conflict-resolution design is scoped with the client.
Configuration.CustomObjectMarkerPatternNote: No vendor-documented naming convention for a customer-created/custom OBJECT (as opposed to a custom FIELD, see CustomFieldModel) was found — the 70-grid catalog is a fixed, vendor-published set; nothing in the corpus describes a mechanism for a brand to define an entirely new grid/object type (only new demographic/interest FIELDS within the existing subscriber-demographic/interest grids). Left null rather than guessed.

Combining two auth models and two directions in one connector would be incoherent; recorded as a known sibling for a future dedicated build.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.namespace: help-centre sections: Aptify, iMIS, netFORUM, Nimble AMS, Personify, Protech, Salesforce, YourMembership, Impexium, Fonteva, Rhythm, Novi, NOAH, Altai, ClearVantage, Timberlake, MemberSuite, Association Anywhere, Microsoft Dynamics 365
OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: These ~20 help-centre sections document how a PARTICULAR AMS is wired to Informz (field mappings, sync cadence, setup steps). They describe deployments, not API objects, and contain no additional grid tokens or actions. Recorded as informational so the universe count stays honest while they stay out of the record model.

The API documents an optional encrypted/compressed message envelope. It is a transport option over the SAME documents, not an object family. Recorded as awareness; implemented only if extraction proves it is required rather than optional (it is not, for plaintext HTTPS).

Landing pages and web forms are rendered surfaces; the AAPI exposes their USAGE as grids (form usage, landing-page summaries, web tracking) — those grids ARE in scope. The rendering surfaces themselves carry no durable syncable records.

Configuration.OutOfScopeReconciliationNote: Reconciled against this build's own SourceAuditor corpus walk (SOURCE_STUDY.md Step 6 'OUT-OF-SCOPE sibling families'): the two families independently found there (Push API v2 — 13 stub objects; the 24 per-AMS partner-guide sections) are already represented above (items 1 and 5). No additional out-of-scope family was found in the pinned 212-article corpus beyond what is listed here. Everything else documented in the corpus (all 70 grids, all 9 actions, all mechanics/glossary articles) IS in scope for this build — no grid and no documented action was excluded.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: Higher Logic validates the Brand id against a registered IP address on every request (API General Information, 360033049191); no live call succeeds from an unregistered egress IP.
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: Live verification/testing is gated on a Higher Logic support case to register the test/CI egress IP, not on credentials alone.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: No describe-all/introspection endpoint exists; the 70-grid/9-action catalog is the vendor's published documentation, not a live per-credential capability list.
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: Discovery-time absence of a grid/action/field must never cause the connector to deactivate that object — see DiscoveryIsAuthoritative.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: StartRow/NumberOfRows is offset-based; concurrent inserts/deletes on the underlying table shift row positions across the page boundary between requests.
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: Deep full-scan completeness is best-effort, mitigated by always pinning a stable SortField, but is never claimed as exact/atomic.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: subscriber_mailing_history exposes only the trailing 100-day window; subscriber_mailing_history_all is its complement (strictly older than 100 days), not a superset.
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: A sync that reads only subscriber_mailing_history silently truncates history beyond 100 days; the connector must declare, per this family, whether it reads one or both grids.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: The demographic-field and interest-name set differs per Informz Brand (tenant) and is not part of the fixed API contract.
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: Field/interest-name absence at runtime for a given credential proves nothing about the vendor's capability — it reflects that brand's own configuration, handled via runtime custom-field discovery, never a vendor-wide Declared column.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: No numeric per-app request-rate cap or rate-limit window is published anywhere in the 212-article corpus (only the 1,000-row-per-request paging cap, which is a page-size limit, not a rate limit).
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: The connector must honour any 429/Retry-After-equivalent signal it observes live and back off adaptively, rather than trusting a declared numeric budget that does not exist. Root Integration.BatchMaxRequestCount / BatchRequestWaitTime are left unset (vendor default, no limit) rather than fabricated.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: No grid returns a general 'subscriber deleted/purged' feed. The only deletion-SHAPED signals in the whole catalog (get_subscriber_interest_changes' Added/Removed event log; subscriber_interests_deleted) are scoped to Interest/target-group MEMBERSHIP changes, not the subscriber record's own lifecycle.
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: Orphan-deletion / tombstone-based sync logic cannot be built for the core subscriber object from documented grids; only Interest-association removal is observable.

fields.Description: Informz AAPI GridRequest "mailing_activity_bounces" — Grid Requests Usage Pattern; GridRequests - Mailing Activity Bounces; Grid Request Usage Pattern. 10 documented Data Elements.

Configuration.gridTypeWireNote: The EXACT case-sensitive string the connector must place in <Grid type="...">. Two vendor-doc casing variants were folded upstream (Mailing_Folder/MailingFolder → mailing_folder; Mailing_Instance → mailing_instance) — see SOURCE_STUDY.md Step 2.
Configuration.taxonomyCitation: GridRequests - Mailing Activity Bounces (360032692292); GridRequests - Subscriber Mailing Activity (360032692492)

accessPath.note: Every grid is a DEPTH-0 door on this vendor: one SOAP operation PostInformzMessage(string) carries a GridRequest document whose <Grid type> selects the record set. The GridResponse returns a FLAT <Record>/<Fields>/<Field element> row set — there are no nested record-collections anywhere in the contract (verified programmatically: zero array/object/$ref properties across all 70 schemas).

Configuration.readMethodEvidence: Single-door SOAP: every read is an HTTP POST of a GridRequest XML document to /aapi/InformzService.svc (operation PostInformzMessage). Declared so T7 compares POST against the derived spec instead of its REST-biased GET default.

watermark.deferredReason: PROVEN NEGATIVE: the typed Data-Element table for this grid declares ZERO DateTime-typed columns, so the vendor exposes no incremental cursor for it.

pk.evidence: KEYLESS (PROVEN NEGATIVE) — grid "mailing_activity_bounces" has NO vendor-declared per-row identity. Source: 360032692292 — "GridRequests - Mailing Activity Bounces" (https://support.higherlogic.com/hc/en-us/articles/360032692292), table 1 of 9 (1 header + 9 data rows, all 9 emitted fields present). The vendor marks a real key explicitly — "Unique <X> ID" in the Description column of a grid's Data-Element table (88 occurrences across 23 of the 212 pinned help-centre articles). In this grid's table that marker appears on exactly one row, mailing_instance_id, where it names the MailingInstance ENTITY's identity (that IO's own Convergent PK, reused across 14 grids) — i.e. a foreign key, not this grid's row key. No column of this grid is marked as this grid's own identity. WITHIN-ARTICLE proven negative: the same article documents 9 grids in 9 tables, and table 2 (mailing_activity_clicks) opens with "Id | Int | True | Unique Link ID" — when a row identity exists this vendor publishes it as a bare Id column in this very article. The bounces table has no Id column at all. user_id is captioned "Remote Application User ID" — no "Unique" marker, and semantically a partner-AMS-supplied value absent by definition for brands running no remote-app integration (corpus-wide it carries an FK on 0 of 18 occurrences; no User IO exists). Refuted empirically by the vendor-derived fixtures (53 rows, bounces-page1 + bounces-page2): mailing_instance_id is 53/53 populated but has only 2 DISTINCT values (1297945 x27, 478933 x26), so it is not a valid sole key either; user_id is 0/53 populated (self-closing empty element); the composite collapses 53 rows to 2 distinct ExternalIDs. The full row is 53/53 distinct, so content-hash identity is valid and lossless. is_repeat_bounce exists precisely to mark a second bounce for the same recipient on the same mailing instance, so the pair cannot be unique by construction. Cross-checked: sources/informz-aapi-openapi.derived.json schema "mailing_activity_bounces" has x-primary-key=null and required=null; a corpus-wide scan for any bounce row identity token (bounce_id, bounces_id, "bounce id", "Unique bounce", activity_id, row_id, record_id) returns 0 hits across all 212 articles. The prior R7 "dimensional grain" key was INFERRED, not sourced — its own evidence string conceded "not a vendor-declared identity" — and it caused a CONFIRMED runtime failure (HybridE2E: 53 of 248 rows failed, "no rows returned from SQL", because the always-empty PK part user_id never reaches the INSERT parameter list). It is removed as a fabrication. Deferred to runtime D4: InformzConnector.BuildRecord already falls back to computeContentHash(raw) over the full row when no PK is declared, so the grid stays syncable and dedupable keyless, and DiscoverFieldsViaFetch/pickKeyFromStats may promote a data-proven soft key once a live sample exists. All 9 fields are IsReadOnly and the object is non-writable, so the Postgres keyless-save failure mode cannot arise.

accessPath.note: Every grid is a DEPTH-0 door on this vendor: one SOAP operation PostInformzMessage(string) carries a GridRequest document whose <Grid type> selects the record set. The GridResponse returns a FLAT <Record>/<Fields>/<Field element> row set — there are no nested record-collections anywhere in the contract (verified programmatically: zero array/object/$ref properties across all 70 schemas).

Configuration.readMethodEvidence: Single-door SOAP: every read is an HTTP POST of a GridRequest XML document to /aapi/InformzService.svc (operation PostInformzMessage). Declared so T7 compares POST against the derived spec instead of its REST-biased GET default.

pk.evidence: PK — INFERRED dimensional grain (WEAK provenance, soft key), not a vendor-declared identity: grid "mailing_activity_challenge" documents no row identity anywhere in its typed Data-Element table or in the 212-article corpus. Grain derived by the catalog-wide R7 motif (mode=typed-reference-and-dimension) over the vendor's own Data-Element table: challenge_id + mailing_instance_id + user_id. Excluded from the grain: tenant scope (brand_id), measure/aggregate columns, descriptive attribute columns functionally dependent on a reference already in the key. Emitted rather than deferred because a PK-less object is silently skipped by CodeGen ("No primary key found" — CodeGenLib/src/Database/manage-metadata.ts::shouldCreateNewEntity), which would drop the object entirely; the key is SOFT (no DB PRIMARY KEY/UNIQUE is generated) so a wrong grain cannot reject a row. Refine at runtime from data statistics.

pk.evidence: KEYLESS (PROVEN NEGATIVE) — grid "web_tracking_summary_demo" has NO vendor-declared per-row identity. Source: 360032692252 — "GridRequests - Landing Pages and Web Tracking Summaries" (https://support.higherlogic.com/hc/en-us/articles/360032692252). The article contains ZERO <table> elements: all five web-tracking/landing summary grids are documented ONLY as <ReturnFields> samples, with no types, no descriptions and no identity marker anywhere. The grain columns (month, year, category, action, type, name, sku) are period/dimension captions, not a declared row key. The vendor marks a real key explicitly — "Unique <X> ID" in the Description column of a grid's Data-Element table (19 of the 212 pinned help-centre articles, 95 occurrences). That marker is ABSENT here. Cross-checked: sources/informz-aapi-openapi.derived.json schema "web_tracking_summary_demo" carries no x-primary-key and no required[]; the token appears in exactly 1 of the 212 pinned articles (corpus-wide scan), and a live re-fetch on 2026-09-08 returned a body byte-identical to the pinned snapshot. The prior R7 "dimensional grain" key was INFERRED, not sourced, and is removed as a fabrication. Deferred to runtime D4: InformzConnector.BuildRecord already falls back to computeContentHash(raw) when no PK is declared, so the grid stays syncable and dedupable keyless, and DiscoverFieldsViaFetch/pickKeyFromStats may promote a data-proven soft key once a live sample exists. Object is read-only, so a keyless entity is never saved.
